READ FIRST, in this order — binding contract:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — tokens, components, and an AUDITED table of what does NOT exist.
2. `app/globals.css` — "KODELY PRODUCT SURFACE" and "PRODUCT UTILITIES" blocks.
3. `components/ui/*` — especially `EmptyState`, `Card`, `Badge`, `Input`/`Textarea`, `Button`. Import them; never hand-roll a second version.
4. `components/app/AppShell.tsx`, `components/app/nav.ts`, `app/(portal)/layout.tsx` — your pages render CONTENT ONLY.

YOU OWN: `app/support/` — **wait, no**: create `app/(portal)/support/`, plus `app/(portal)/dashboard/domains/` and `app/(portal)/dashboard/integrations/`. All three are new. Do NOT touch other portal pages, `components/**`, or `lib/**`. Other agents are working in parallel.

Your three pages are the hardest ones in this redesign, because **all three sit on top of almost nothing**. The whole job is to make each one genuinely useful and completely honest, instead of a mock. Read the honesty rule at the bottom of `docs/design-system.md` before you start.

## PAGE 1 — Support (`/support`)

What exists:
- An **unauthenticated contact form → email**: `app/api/contact/route.ts`, gated on `isMailConfigured()`. Read it in full — you can reuse the endpoint, but check whether it is rate-limited and whether it accepts an authenticated user's identity.
- **Build feedback** thumbs up/down: `app/api/feedback/route.ts` — writes an `Event` only. **There is no reply path.** Anyone who leaves feedback expecting an answer is currently getting nothing back.
- `components/marketing/ContactForm.tsx` — read it, do not edit it.

What does NOT exist: any ticket model, ticket status, or conversation history. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and `prisma/schema.prisma:219-232` says explicitly it is "Never shown to the customer" — do NOT surface it. There is no support AI assistant.

Build the best real support page possible: a proper authenticated contact form (prefilled with their email, and able to reference a specific site of theirs, which genuinely helps), clear expectations about how they get a reply, and honest self-serve help. **Do not build a fake ticket list, fake ticket statuses, or a chat window with no backend.** If `isMailConfigured()` is false, the page must say what to do instead rather than showing a form that silently fails.

The brief asked for a "Kodely AI Assistant" here. Do not fake one. Report what building a real one would actually take.

## PAGE 2 — Domains (`/dashboard/domains`)

What exists: **nothing** for custom domains. No `Domain` model, no `customDomain` field, no DNS/CNAME/SSL/ACME code, no purchase flow. The host allowlist is hard-coded to three shapes in `app/api/site/[slug]/site-host.ts:68-76`. The SEO content on the live site even states custom domains are unsupported (`content/seo/ai-website-builder-vs-hiring-a-web-designer.json:29`).

What DOES exist and is genuinely useful: every published project has a real working address. `Project.slug` → `https://<slug>.kodely.site` (built at `app/api/projects/[id]/publish/route.ts:180-183`; staging uses the path form). Read `site-host.ts` and the publish route to get this exactly right.

So build a page that is actually worth visiting: list every site with its real live address, published status, copy-link, and open. Then a clear, honest section on custom domains stating that they are not supported yet and what will be needed. **Do not build a "Connect domain" form that goes nowhere.** Note the slug is deliberately never regenerated on rename (`app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:49-73`) — read why, and tell the customer, because it explains why their URL does not change.

## PAGE 3 — Integrations (`/dashboard/integrations`)

There is nothing customer-facing. The only external services are Stripe, Google sign-in, Discord OAuth for a one-off reward, and nodemailer — none user-configurable. `checkIntegrations()` in `app/admin/health/checks.ts:201` is an admin env-var check, not a feature.

This page is marked `soon: true` in `components/app/nav.ts`. Make it a genuinely honest, well-designed "not yet" page that is still worth landing on: say what is not there, and point at what IS connected to their account today where that is true and user-visible (e.g. Google sign-in if that is how they signed in; a Discord reward link if configured — check `app/api/rewards/**` for what is real and conditional). Verify each claim in code before you print it.

HARD RULES:
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** This is the entire point of your three pages.
- No new npm dependencies. Server Components by default; `"use client"` only where interaction needs it.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element, `k-num` on figures.
- Any form must handle its failure states truthfully, including the not-configured case.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on your paths with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.
- Copy matters more than usual here. Write from the customer's side of the screen. No apologies, no vagueness, no "coming soon!" with an exclamation mark — say what is true and what they can do instead.

REPORT BACK: what you built, every claim you verified in code (with `file:line`), what you refused to fake, what a real AI support assistant and real custom domains would each actually require, and anything untested.

53	
54	`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl` (8/10/14/20/28px) · `shadow-e1|e2|e3` ·
55	`duration-[var(--t-1)]` 120ms, `--t-2` 200ms, `--t-3` 380ms ·
56	`ease-[var(--ease)]`
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Utility classes
61	
62	`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`.
101	
102	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
103	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
108	
109	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
110	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
111	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
112	
113	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
114	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
115	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
116	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
117	and not a progress bar.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
122	
123	| Thing | Reality |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
126	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
127	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
128	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
129	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
130	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
131	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
132	| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
133	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
134	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
135	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
136	
137	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, ARE cheaply real** — the
138	`Session` model is per-user and queryable.
139	
140	### The rule
141	
142	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
143	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
144	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

1	// WHICH HOSTS MAY SERVE A CUSTOMER'S GENERATED HTML.
2	//
3	// The site route renders arbitrary attacker-authored markup with
4	// `Content-Type: text/html` and a CSP whose `'self'` resolves to whatever host
5	// the request arrived on. On <slug>.kodely.site that is exactly right: the page
6	// is first-party to its own site and to nothing else. On kodely.me it is a
7	// first-party page on the application's own origin, with a real certificate and
8	// the real domain in the address bar — a phishing surface. Nothing in the route
9	// or the proxy used to look at the Host header at all, so
10	// https://kodely.me/api/site/<any-published-slug>/ served that page to anyone.
11	//
12	// This is an ALLOWLIST, not a block on the app domain. A blocklist would have
13	// to enumerate every name the app answers to (apex, www, the admin host, any
14	// future one) and would fail open the moment one was added.
15	//
16	// The `/api/site/<slug>` path form is NOT the bug and is not removed: staging
17	// depends on it, because there is no wildcard DNS for *.kodely.site off prod, so
18	// staging.kodely.me/api/site/<slug> is the only way to look at a published site
19	// there. lib/site-seo.ts derives canonical and og:url from precisely this
20	// subdomain-vs-path distinction, and both forms below keep producing the URL
21	// they produced before.
22	
23	const SITES_BASE = (process.env.KODELY_SITES_BASE ?? "kodely.site").trim().toLowerCase();
24	
25	// Where the path form stays legitimate. Overridable so a second staging
26	// environment does not need a code change; the default is what deploy.sh
27	// deploys and verifies.
28	const STAGING_HOST = (process.env.KODELY_STAGING_HOST ?? "staging.kodely.me").trim().toLowerCase();
29	
30	/** Host header minus the port, lowercased. Handles bracketed IPv6 literals. */
31	export function bareHost(host: string): string {
32	  const h = host.trim().toLowerCase();
33	  const v6 = h.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]/);
34	  if (v6) return v6[1];
35	  return h.split(":")[0];
36	}
37	
38	function isLoopback(bare: string): boolean {
39	  return (
40	    bare === "localhost" ||
41	    bare.endsWith(".localhost") ||
42	    bare === "127.0.0.1" ||
43	    bare === "::1"
44	  );
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * May this Host serve the published site `slug`?
49	 *
50	 * Three shapes, and nothing else:
51	 *
52	 *  1. `<slug>.kodely.site` — the branded subdomain, which proxy.ts rewrites to
53	 *     this route. Note it must match THIS slug: `a.kodely.site/api/site/b/` is
54	 *     refused. That is not the reported finding, but it is the same mistake one
55	 *     level down — it would let any customer host any other customer's page on
56	 *     their own site's origin, where `'self'` and `frame-ancestors 'self'` both
57	 *     resolve to the victim site's name. The legitimate rewrite always agrees
58	 *     with the subdomain, so nothing real is affected.
59	 *  2. The staging host, on the path form, because staging has no wildcard DNS.
60	 *     Staging is not the application's public identity; a page served there is
61	 *     not a credible impersonation of kodely.me, and reaching it means the
62	 *     victim already accepted a staging URL.
63	 *  3. Loopback, so local development and `next start` testing keep working.
64	 *
65	 * Everything else — kodely.me, www, the admin host, any bare IP, any Host a
66	 * caller invents — is refused.
67	 */
68	export function siteHostAllowed(host: string, slug: string): boolean {
69	  const bare = bareHost(host);
70	  if (!bare) return false;
71	
72	  const wanted = slug.trim().toLowerCase();
73	  if (wanted && bare === `${wanted}.${SITES_BASE}`) return true;
74	  if (bare === STAGING_HOST) return true;
75	  return isLoopback(bare);
76	}

## What I built

Six new files, all inside the three directories I own:

- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\support\page.tsx` + `ContactPanel.tsx`
- `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\domains\page.tsx` + `address.ts` + `CopyAddress.tsx`

Nothing outside those paths was touched. All content-only pages (no nav, no background, no second `ToastProvider`); Server Components except `ContactPanel` and `CopyAddress`.

**Support** — a real authenticated contact form posting to the existing `/api/contact`, prefilled with the account email (editable, labelled "Reply to"), plus a `<Select>` of the user's own sites. Choosing one prepends verified server-computed context (site name, real public address, published/draft, builder URL) to the message body so support never has to ask for it. Then: "How you get a reply" (email only, no ticket list, no published SLA, no chat, no AI assistant), an explicit card saying the build thumbs-up/down is *not* a message to us, nine `<details>` self-serve answers each traced to code, and four "before you write" links.

**Domains** — every project with its real address, Live/Draft badge, published date, copy-to-clipboard, Open (published only), Edit/Publish. Then "Your address never changes" explaining the no-re-slug rule in the customer's terms, then an `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` for custom domains with what it means today and what the feature would need.

**Integrations** — a lead `EmptyState kind="unavailable"`, then "Already connected to your account" rendered from live values (sign-in method from the user row, SMTP, Stripe, published-site forms with a real submission count, Discord only when configured), then an eight-item "what Kodely does not connect to" list.

## What I refused to fake

- No ticket list, ticket statuses, conversation history, or in-app inbox. No `SupportNote` surfaced anywhere (`prisma/schema.prisma:219-232`).
- No AI support assistant and no chat window. The page says so in one sentence rather than staying silent.
- No response-time promise. The page states there isn't one and tells the customer to say if something is time-critical.
- No "Connect domain" form, no DNS/CNAME instructions, no verification stepper.
- No integrations directory, no toggles, no "Connect" buttons, no greyed-out logo grid of services we don't integrate with.
- No `soon`-style optimism copy. No exclamation marks.
- When `isMailConfigured()` is false the support form is **not rendered at all** — replaced by an `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and a prefilled `mailto:` to `CONTACT_TO`, which does not depend on this server. ## What a real AI support assistant would take

The hard part isn't the model, it's the grounding and the blast radius:

1. **Retrieval over truth, not marketing.** Today's honest answers live in code comments (`route.ts:49-73`, `_lib.ts`, `site-forms.ts`). Those would need to become a maintained, versioned answer corpus, or the assistant confidently tells people custom domains work.
2. **Scoped read access to the asking user's own state** — balance, ledger, build history including failure reasons, publish/moderation findings, project slugs. That's a new authorization surface: an assistant that can read one user's data is one prompt-injection away from reading another's, and generated site content (attacker-authored) is already in the database.
3. **A handoff path.** An assistant with no escalation is worse than a form. That means the ticket model that deliberately does not exist: a thread, a status, a reply the customer can read in-app.
4. **Refusal discipline and cost.** It must say "I don't know, here's a human" for anything about money, deletion, or moderation, and every conversation is metered spend against a product whose unit economics are already a per-build ledger.
5. **Evaluation.** No test suite currently asserts anything about answer correctness. Shipping this without one converts a support channel into a source of confident wrong answers.

Estimate: the ticket model + reply path is the prerequisite and is the bigger half; the assistant on top is meaningless without it.

## What real custom domains would take

1. **Schema and ownership**: a `Domain` model (`userId`, `projectId`, hostname, verification token, state) plus a DNS TXT/CNAME verification check. Hostnames are globally unique and adversarial — verification is the security boundary, not a formality.
2. **Certificates**: ACME issuance and unattended renewal per customer domain, with rate-limit handling against Let's Encrypt, plus somewhere to store keys. This is the part that silently breaks at 90 days.
3. **Edge/DNS routing**: today `*.kodely.site` is a single wildcard nginx block pointing at prod only (`publish/route.ts:16-24`). Arbitrary customer domains need a per-host route and a cert lookup at TLS handshake time.
